_meta.source: Bureau of Indian Standards IS 10500:2012; CGWB Ground Water Year Book; WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality (4th ed., 2017)
_meta.note: Permissible limits per BIS 10500:2012. Health effects summarised from WHO and ICMR guidance.

fluoride.name: Fluoride
fluoride.natural_origin: Leaching from fluoride-bearing rocks (granite, gneiss). Worsened by over-extraction of groundwater.
health_effects: Dental fluorosis (mottled teeth) above 1.5 mg/L
Skeletal fluorosis (joint pain, bone deformity) with chronic exposure above 3 mg/L
Children most vulnerable
treatment_household: Activated alumina filters (Nalgonda technique scaled down)
Reverse osmosis (RO) — effective but wastes water and removes essential minerals
restoration_programmes: Jal Jeevan Mission — fluoride priority habitations

arsenic.name: Arsenic
arsenic.natural_origin: Reductive dissolution from alluvial sediments in Ganga–Brahmaputra basin. A geogenic contaminant, not industrial.
health_effects: Arsenicosis: skin lesions, hyperpigmentation, keratosis
Group 1 carcinogen — skin, lung, bladder cancers
Cardiovascular and developmental effects
treatment_household: Nano-composite filters approved under Jal Jeevan Mission
treatment_community: Switching to surface water sources where feasible
Deep tubewells tapping arsenic-free aquifers (with monitoring)
restoration_programmes: Jal Jeevan Mission — arsenic-affected habitation priority
State arsenic task forces (West Bengal, Bihar)

nitrate.name: Nitrate
nitrate.natural_origin: Anthropogenic: agricultural fertiliser runoff, septic tanks, livestock waste. Not geogenic.
health_effects: Methaemoglobinaemia (blue-baby syndrome) in infants under 6 months
Possible link to gastric cancer with chronic exposure
Pregnant women advised caution
treatment_household: Boiling does NOT remove nitrate — it can concentrate it
treatment_community: Source protection: setback distances around wells, fertiliser regulation
restoration_programmes: Atal Bhujal Yojana — demand-side groundwater management

iron.name: Iron
iron.natural_origin: Naturally occurring in groundwater across north-east India and laterite belts. Aesthetic and secondary health concern.
health_effects: Generally not a primary health hazard at typical levels
Stains laundry, plumbing; metallic taste
Very high chronic intake linked to haemochromatosis in susceptible individuals
treatment_household: Iron removal filters using birm/manganese greensand
restoration_programmes: Jal Jeevan Mission — iron removal plants (IRP) for affected habitations

salinity.name: Salinity (TDS / EC)
salinity.natural_origin: Coastal saline ingress, evaporite deposits in arid zones, over-extraction causing seawater intrusion.
health_effects: High sodium load — hypertension risk
Gastrointestinal irritation at very high TDS
Generally aesthetic (taste) rather than acute toxicity
treatment_community: Surface water transmission from non-saline sources
Managed aquifer recharge to push back saline interface

uranium.name: Uranium
uranium.natural_origin: Geogenic, leaching from uranium-bearing granites. Reported in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana.
health_effects: Chemical toxicity to kidneys (primary concern, not radioactivity at these levels)
Long-term low-dose exposure under study

microbial.name: Microbial (E. coli / coliform)
microbial.natural_origin: Faecal contamination from septic tanks, open defecation, leaky sewers, surface runoff into shallow wells.
health_effects: Diarrhoeal disease, cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A/E
Major cause of child mortality in India
Acute, immediate risk — unlike chemical contaminants
treatment_household: Boiling for 1 minute at rolling boil (most reliable)
SODIS (solar disinfection in clear PET bottles, 6 hours)
treatment_community: Source protection: well-head sanitation, setback from latrines
